chunks: It is ordained for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, to make a bequest to the parents and next of kin in a fair manner, as a duty upon the God-conscious.

key_terms.وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ: And the next of kin / close relatives

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on making a will when death approaches?
ai.summary: This verse, known as the 'Verse of Wills' (Ayat al-Wasiyyah), establishes the primary obligation of bequeathing to parents and close relatives before the later revelation of specific inheritance laws (faraid) in Surah An-Nisa. In Shia scholarship, this is often viewed as the foundational rule for voluntary bequests, which remain valid alongside the fixed shares, ensuring that the pious fulfill their duty to family through equitable distribution. The emphasis on 'al-ma'ruf' (goodness/equity) highlights that the will must be executed with fairness and without prejudice, reflecting the piety of the testator.
